Justice J.D. Kapoor (Oral)
1. Complainant
of the appellant seeking replacement of Music System sold by the respondent no. 1 and manufactured
by the respondent No. 2, which was
already a replaced system and was found to be defective, was dismissed vide impugned order dated 20th
October, 2006 passed by the District Forum . Feeling aggrieved the appellant
has preferred this appeal.
2. Allegations
of the respondent, in brief, were that complaint
u/s 12
of the C.P. Act was
earlier filed by appellant on 12.1.2005 which was finally disposed off vide
order dated 14.10.2005 with the
direction to the appellant for replacement of the music system with cost of Rs. 500/-. Respondent again filed complaint alleging that
the replaced system has also giving trouble.
The appellant purchased the music system on 13.11.2004 for Rs. 16,650/-.
3. Appellant
alleged that in the replace music system, FM and other channels did not work
properly and this defect was brought to the notice of the respondent No. 1 on
15.10.2005 but could not remove the defect but asked the appellant to put his
signature on the papers which appellant refused. Again OPs were contacted by
the appellant for the defects in the music system in which even Vividh Bharti Station
was not working properly and this time a person from OP visited him on 21.10.05 but could not
sort things right and thereafter appellant was not being heard by the OPs and
hence a legal notice dated 10.11.2005 through his counsel was sent which also
yielded no results. Hence the appellant preferred the instant complaint seeking
replacement of the system and compensation of Rs. 10,000/- for mental agony, harassment
along litigation cost.
4. As
against this, the respondent No. 2 filed detailed reply wherein proceedings in
an earlier complaint were admitted and it was sated that with the intent to give the appellant a
demonstration of the said new replaced music system, they kept on calling the
appellant but appellant avoided them on
one or the other pretext. In this connection, details regarding contacts made
with the appellant on telephone vide noting made in job sheet dated 19.10.05
were referred to which job card has been placed on record as EX-1. It was pleaded
that finally appellant was offered demonstration on 21.10.2005 but since appellant
was not satisfied with the demonstration, another demonstration was offered
free of cost on 22.10.2005. According to the respondent on all such occasions
including 19/10/2005 appellant did not sign the job sheet.
Subsequently appellant lodged a complaint of some problem and so they sent
their skilled technician on 26.10.05 but appellant refused the skilled
technician to detect the nature of the problem and in this connection appellant
was again contacted on 27.10.05 and appellant
was requested to bring the new set to the authorized service centre for
detection of exact nature of the grievance but appellant till date did not
bother to bring the said new set to their authorized service centre and filed
complained based on false and concocted facts.
5. In
identical cases, we have taken a view that wherever goods sold by trader are held to be defective as defined under
section
2(1)(d)
, the endeavour of the District Forum should be to order for refund of the cost of the goods and
not to replace the defective goods with a new goods free from the defect as possibility
of new goods being not to the satisfaction of the consumer and not being defective
cannot be ruled out and such an order relegates the parties to second bout of
litigation as is the case in hand.
6. After
perusal of the impugned order , we find that the
District Forum advised the appellant to
take system to Respondent No. 2 for
necessary repairs for which necessary direction can be issued. Appellant refused
to take new set to service centre and he only wanted his money back.
7. It
appears that the District Forum did not view the stand of the appellant in the
right perspective by observing that consumer cannot direct according to the
whims and fancies. Consumer disputes are
such, which need speedy, inexpensive and effective remedy.
8.
Section 14(1)(d)
entitles a
consumer to not only an amount of compensation as to the actual loss suffered
by him but also compensation of mental agony, harassment, physical discomfort
and other suffering suffered by the consumer. The word compensation has been
given wide meaning by the Honble Supreme Court in
Ghaziabad Development
Authority Vs Balbir Singh-
(2004) 5
Supreme court Cases 65 . The observation of the Honble Supreme Court are pithy and need
to be reproduced and are as under:
The word compensation is of a very wide connotation. It may constitute
actual loss or expected loss and may extend to compensation for physical,
mental or even emotional suffering, insult or injury or loss. The provisions of
the
Consumer Protection Act
enable a consumer to claim and empower the
Commission to redress any injustice done. The Commission or the Forum is
entitled to award not only value of goods or services but also to compensate a
consumer for injustice suffered by him. The Commission/ Forum must determine
that such sufferance is due to malafide or capricious or oppressive act. It can
then determine amount for which the authority is liable to compensate the
consumer for his sufferance due to misfeasance in public office by the
officers. Such compensation is for vindicating the strength of law.
10. Had
the music system been defect free, complainant would not have taken the trouble
of filing another complaint before the District Forum by incurring more expenses
by engaging lawyer. There are no observations of the District Forum in the
impugned order except that District Forum advised the appellant to take the
system to the respondent no. 1 for removing defects.
11. Quality
of any goods sold by a trader is tested on the anvil of definition of word defect provided by
Section 2(1)(f)
of the consumer
Protection
Act, 1986
which means any fault,
imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or
standard which is required to be maintained by or under any law for the time
being in force. In such an eventuality
there are four options open to the Consumer Forum. First to direct the trader to remove the defect,
second is to replace the goods with new
good with same standard and
specification free from defect, third is
to refund the price to the consumer charged by the trader,
and fourth is to pay an amount as
compensation for any loss injury suffered by the consumer due to negligence of
the OP.
12. Forgoing
reasons persuade us to hold that music system was defective system as projected
by the appellant in various complaints as well through legal notice served upon
respondent no. 1 which was never replied.
13. In the result, we allow the
appeal, set aside the impugned order with the direction to respondent No. 1 to
refund the cost of the music system on return of the same by the appellant and pay Rs.
2500/- as compensation including cost of the litigation with the liberty to reimburse
the same with the manufacturer i.e. respondent no. 2
14. Order
should be complied with within one month after receipt of this order.
15.
 F.D.R./
Bank Guarantee, if any, furnished by the appellant be returned forthwith after
completion of due formalities.
16.
 A copy of this order as
per statutory requirements, be forwarded to the parties free of charge and also to the
concerned District Forum and thereafter the file be consigned to the record
room.
(Justice J.D.
Kapoor)
